references.text: Isaiah 6:1 describes the prophet seeing the Lord, while John 6:46 emphasizes that no one has seen the Father except the one who is from God. This creates a contrast between prophetic vision and Jesus' unique, direct sight of God's nature.
In Exodus 33:20, God says that no human can see His face and live. John 6:46 confirms this impossibility for all others except the Son, who has seen the Father.
Exodus 33:11 mentions that the Lord spoke to Moses face to face, as a friend. This prepares the theme in John 6:46 about the unique relationship and vision that only the Son possesses.
John 1:18 is a direct parallel expressing the same theological point: no one has ever seen God, but the only Son has made Him known.
In John 14:9, Jesus says: "He who has seen me has seen the Father". This is the direct fulfillment of the claim in John 6:46 that the Son has seen the Father.
